title: Budget
description: The context budget one run works under: the provider-independent byte and token limits both the browser and the Desk server read from one table (internal/aicontext/policy.json, ContextPolicy in web/src/assistant/context/policy.ts, aicontext.Policy in Go). The model's context window and output reserve may be overridden per model by the assistant profile (configuration); everything else is fixed. Input bytes for one request are min(maxInputBytes, max(1024, (contextWindowTokens - outputTokens) * 3)); the browser further leaves briefBytes, and memoryBytes where the host has not said memory is off (the run's context.memory, agent#11), a reserve kept from when the server added the brief and memory behind the adapter; since ADR-0005 the adapter places them itself (each held to its bound, $defs/hostPart) and counts them where they sit, and the server refuses before dispatch, never clipping, a request over the input bytes (context-limit, not-started). Open: the Go reader ignores a member it does not name. The request allowance, the grants and the fixed limits are in $defs. The harness adds two time bounds the Desk's table does not carry (packages/harness/context/policy.ts, TIME_DEFAULTS), each taken from the table where it does: turnMilliseconds and toolCallMilliseconds; and three bounds on the Runtime's test tool (TEST_DEFAULTS), likewise: testCallsPerTurn, testPackBytes and testMatrixBytes; and two image bounds (IMAGE_DEFAULTS), likewise: imagesPerRequest and imageBytesPerRequest; and two bounds on the index of earlier results a chat-scoped run's first message carries (INDEX_DEFAULTS, agent#8), likewise: turnIndexEntries and turnIndexBytes; and the bound on the project's own instructions (PROMPT_DEFAULTS, ADR-0005), likewise: projectInstructionsBytes. The table also states the critic's default, adversarialReview (agent#10), which the harness adds to the Desk's table: both engines read it where a session leaves adversarialReview unset.

maxInputBytes.description: Fixed transport ceiling on one request's input, whatever the window.

contextWindowTokens.description: The model's context window, in tokens, for the byte estimate (three bytes a token).

outputTokens.description: The output reserve. A request's own max_tokens, max_completion_tokens or maxOutputTokens raises it up to half the window; above half, the request is refused.

toolResultBytes.description: The largest tool result, as JSON text, the model is shown whole (tool-result.json).

retainedBytes.description: What one execution's context ledger may retain in all.

recentMessages.description: Declared in the table; read by no assistant code today.

historyBytes.description: Declared in the table; read by the server's research worker, not by the assistant loop.

briefBytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes of the project brief the host's brief() may answer (ADR-0005; before it, the most the server added behind the adapter). A longer answer is refused before the run's first request (configuration) and nothing is sent.

memoryBytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes of recalled project memory the host's memoryFor(query) may answer (ADR-0005; before it, the most the server added behind the adapter); a longer answer is refused as a brief's is. The harness leaves it out of a run's input allowance only while memory may be on: a run whose host says memory is off (context.memory: false, agent#11) reserves none, has the full allowance and asks memoryFor nothing; absent, the reserve stays (contextPolicy in packages/harness/context/policy.ts).

turnMilliseconds.description: One turn's wall clock, from the run's start, on the vercel engine: when it passes, what is in flight is stopped and the run pauses as budget_paused does, with its checkpoint and a reason; a proposal already made is delivered, with a note, and the run ends. Continuing the pause takes a request grant, so at the 100-request cap it cannot be continued; the reason says so. The codex engine has none of its own (the Codex bridge bounds a run at ten minutes). Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 900000 (fifteen minutes).

toolCallMilliseconds.description: One runtime or host tool call's deadline, on both engines: a call past it is no longer waited for (it may still complete; a host tool is also handed the deadline's abort signal) and is answered to the model as a failed result (failure code timeout, source tool, outcome unknown), and the run goes on. propose_pack, which the adapter reads itself, and a tool that pauses the run for the person or the coordinator have none. Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 120000 (two minutes).

imagesPerRequest.description: The most images one model request carries, on the vercel engine (agent#5): the newest; an older image past it is replaced in that request by a line saying it is no longer shown, and the result that brought it still describes it. The codex engine's agent wire carries text and shows none. Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 8.

imageBytesPerRequest.description: The most bytes, decoded, of the images one model request carries, counted from the newest with imagesPerRequest; an older image that would pass it is replaced by the same line. Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 16777216 (16 MiB, one image at its own bound).

testCallsPerTurn.description: How many experimental_test_cases calls one turn may make, on both engines (context/session.ts, claimTestCall). Each call re-sends the whole pack, so a test, fix and retest loop is held to a few rounds rather than to the request allowance. A call past it is not made: the model reads a failed result (failure code tool-failed, source tool, outcome not-started) naming the limit, and the run goes on. Counted per turn: the count is the checkpoint's testCalls (checkpoint.json), carried as used is through a Retry, a budget continuation and a delegation's parent continuation, and the delegation coordinator counts the parent and its continuation together; a new turn starts at nought. Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 3.

testPackBytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes experimental_test_cases' pack text may be; the tool gate refuses a larger call on the wire (tool-call.json $defs/testCasesArguments). Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 65536.

testMatrixBytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes experimental_test_cases' matrix text may be; the tool gate refuses a larger call on the wire. Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 65536.

adversarialReview.description: Whether the critic runs where a session leaves adversarialReview unset, on both engines (packages/harness/refutation.ts, criticRuns): false, so a critic runs only where the host asks for one, at any reasoning tier. The harness adds it to the Desk's table (contract/desk/policy.json). The host chooses per run by passing adversarialReview on the session, from its own settings; this member is the default the harness reads where a session leaves it unset.

turnIndexEntries.description: How many earlier results the index a chat-scoped run's first message carries lists, the newest; older ones are counted in its omitted member (tool-result.json#/$defs/turnIndex, agent#8). Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 20.

turnIndexBytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes that index may be, its line and data block together (agent#8). It is also cut to the room the run's first message leaves in the prompt's allowance, and to at most a quarter of that allowance (INDEX_SHARE): rows go, oldest first, until it fits, an index with no room is not sent, and the request is never previewed and a run never fails because of it. Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 8000.

projectInstructionsBytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes of the project's own instructions the host's projectInstructions() may answer (ADR-0005): instructions at the lowest rank, placed after the package's guidance and the brief. A longer answer is refused before the run's first request (configuration) and nothing is sent. Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 4000.

modelBudget.description: One model's override (ModelContextBudget). Closed: both readers refuse another member.

outputTokens.description: At least 1024 and at most half the window.

configuration.description: The assistant profile's context member (ContextConfiguration; aicontext.Configuration). Closed: contextConfiguration refuses another member and the Go decoder disallows unknown fields. projectBrief is a relative project file the host reads for its brief() answer, once per run (ADR-0005; before it, the server read it afresh on every dispatch); models holds at most 128 overrides by model name.

projectBrief.description: A relative project file: no backslash, colon, CR, LF or NUL, and no empty, . or .. segment.

propertyNames.description: A model name: trimmed, with no CR, LF or NUL.

requestAllowance.description: What the host tells the model about the request allowance, inside its execution guidance (ExecutionController.guidance): the counts where the host counts model requests, or a note where the provider manages its own loop. In a conversation the delegation coordinator wraps, the same state carries toolCalls beside it ($defs/toolCallAllowance). Written for the model; no reader.

toolCallAllowance.description: The tool-call cap the execution state states as toolCalls (agent#13), where the delegation coordinator holds one (ExecutionController.toolAllowance): scope response, the MAX_TOOLS (20) host and Runtime tool calls one response may make, the parent's and its delegated children's together; scope task, one child's own budget (delegated-task.json#/$defs/budget). The context tools are not counted. Absent from a run the coordinator does not wrap. Written for the model; no reader.

budgetIncreaseAnswer.description: The answer of the host tool request_budget_increase. It never grants: approval-required pauses the run (budget_paused) for the person; within-allowance tells the model to carry on (more than two requests remain); unavailable is the provider-managed case.

deskLimits.description: The fixed limits, by the Desk's own constant names, at the pinned commit. Values the Desk writes as unnamed literals are stated in these descriptions instead: a checkpoint holds at most 8 grants; one delegation batch has one to three tasks; on an agent capability the delegation coordinator admits at most 5 agent runs in all, shared by the parent and its children, retries every agent run under it, the parent's included, after a busy, not-started refusal, three attempts in all, and runs one child at a time (two on a model capability); the Codex bridge bounds an agent run at ten minutes (internal/codexbridge/run.go), which the server reports as a timeout failure; the browser's agent transport ends a run at twelve minutes, a backstop behind the bridge's deadline, and refuses a frame over 2 MiB, more than 8 MiB received or 64 queued frames, and more than 20 tool calls; the Codex bridge allows two recovery notices (retry events) per run; the model relay bounds one relayed request at ten minutes and two minutes idle (relayDeadline, relayIdle), and has no deadline for a whole run. This harness (agent#13, agent#15) keeps MAX_TOOLS and RESULT_LIMIT, states MAX_TOOLS to the model (toolCallAllowance), keeps a result over the limit whole in the chat's ledger rather than failing the task, and replaces MAX_CHILD_MODELS, MAX_CHILD_TOOLS and CHILD_TIMEOUT with each profile's budget (delegated-task.json#/$defs/profile); the Desk's values stay stated here as the Desk's.

MAX_TURNS.description: The first request allowance of a model-requests execution (web/src/assistant/engines/contract.ts).

MAX_REQUEST_ALLOWANCE.description: The most requests any execution may be granted (execution/state.ts).

MAX_CHECKPOINT_BYTES.description: The largest checkpoint, as JSON text (execution/state.ts).

MAX_TOOLS.description: Tool calls a delegation shares across the parent and its children (delegation.ts).

MAX_CHILD_MODELS.description: Model requests one child may make (delegation.ts).

MAX_CHILD_TOOLS.description: Tool calls one child may make (delegation.ts).

CHILD_TIMEOUT.description: One child's time limit, in milliseconds (delegation.ts).

maxConversationBytes.description: The largest saved chat history document, all chats of a project (internal/desk/conversations.go).

MaxPromptBytes.description: The largest prompt on the agent wire (internal/codexbridge/contract.go); the instructions are held to the same number as a literal.

stateLocation.description: Where the execution state sits in one request on one wire (agent#9). The state is one text: the header, then the request counters ($defs/requestAllowance, and in a conversation the delegation coordinator wraps the tool-call cap, $defs/toolCallAllowance), plan and operations index the model is told, the host's changing text and the step's own instruction. It is the text at pointer (a JSON pointer into the provider body the adapter composed) from the header, which starts a line, to the end of that text; the header occurs nowhere else in the request. The critic's step note carries the same header. The state is the eighth layer of the request (ADR-0005): after the stable prefix (the package's guidance and the host's parts, $defs/hostPart), the history and the tools. On the agent wire (the Codex engine) the run is one request with one prompt string: the request text, then a chat's index of earlier results, then, after a blank line, the header, the host's changing text and, in a conversation, the execution guidance (agent#36). No host reads a request to find anything in it (ADR-0005 removed the recall rule).

thinking.description: The run's thinking tier, as far as it chooses the placement.

capabilities.description: What the host said about the endpoint: members of its capability record (capability.json), of which the placement reads statePlacement and strictAlternation.

placement.description: The placement the capabilities and the tier resolve to.

request.description: Which request of the run, counted from 1.

header.const: EXECUTION STATE (from the host, current for this request and replaced on the next; working state, not a message from the person and never approval)

hostPart.description: One of the host's parts of every request (ADR-0005; packages/harness/prompt.ts, HOST_PARTS): the member it is, the layer it is placed in, the host's injection point that answers it, the first and last lines of its block and the member of this table that bounds it. The adapter asks each injection point once per run, before its first request (memoryFor with the person's message, or a delegated child's objective, and not where the host said memory is off), and places each part it answered in the system text (the agent wire's instructions) after the package's guidance, in layer order, a blank line before each block: the header, the text, the end line. A part answered with nothing is left out; one that is not text, or is over its bound, is refused and the run fails before any request (configuration). The project's instructions are instructions at the lowest rank: they follow the package's guidance, and they cannot grant a tool or change an effect, because the offer and the gate are code. The system text through the last part is the request's stable prefix: the same bytes on every request of the run.

layer.description: The part's layer of the request: 3 the brief, 4 the project's instructions, 5 the memory, after 1 the package's guidance and 2 the Runtime's prompt (which reaches the adapter with the person's request as one text and is sent where the request goes).

injection.description: The host's injection point (host.ts, HarnessHost; the Go adapter.Run's Host).

bound.description: The member of this table that bounds the part's UTF-8 bytes.
